newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen parliament approves $5 bln natgas project.
newsitem.headline: Yemen parliament approves $5 bln natgas project.

text.p: Yemen's parliament on Tuesday gave its stamp of approval to a $5 billion foreign-backed liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in the Gulf state.
A parliamentary statement said a majority of members had approved the LNG project which was signed in January.

Under that agreement France's Total SA will take a 36 percent stake in the project, U.S. Exxon Corp jointly with Hunt Oil 30 percent, South Korea's Yukong eight percent and the Yemeni government 26 percent.
First exports from the Yemen Liquefied Natural Gas Co project are slated for 2001 and will have to compete against rival LNG projects in Qatar, Oman and Abu Dhabi for gas markets.
Yemen Liquefied Natural Gas Company plans to produce an annual five million tonnes of LNG.
Paris-based Total and Turkey's national gas company BOTAS signed an agreement last year to negotiate the terms of a 25-year LNG supply contract of an annual 2.6 million tonnes.
Yemeni oil and minerals resources minister Mohammad Said al-Attar was reported in January as saying that Yemen planned to cut its stake in the project to only 15 percent.
Presidential approval is required for the project's final go-ahead.
